chapter: Jelly Roll's road trip, Benny Carter and Chick Webb
title: The decline of clarinet players and his views on rock and roll
summary: Procope laments there are few clarinetists now, dismisses rock and roll's saxophone playing, and is optimistic about young people discovering jazz.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: No, because -- because -- that's another thing, musicians are not like they used to be. Now they get a saxophone and they have it awhile and they honk, honk, honk, and that's it. There's no depth. You know, they get out of here with a so-called rock and roll. I think the name rock and roll is just a -- is just a subterfuge to cover up for something that's not happening. Because there's nothing really happening in rock and roll. Some. Of course there's good in everything, you know, like you'll get a good tune, or a hit tune out of rock and roll once in awhile, but I don't believe that it's contributed anything to jazz, to jazz music. And it's not jazz. It's not all jazz. It's guitars and whatever, and you get these saxophone players, and just like they say about the guitar players, you know, you learn three or four chords and you'll have four or five notes you can honk on the saxophone and that's it.
Well, we won't even go into that, about the electronics. So I was saying that the clarinet players,

you know, there were a whole lot of clarinet players in those days. You know, almost every band had a couple of clarinet players who could play the clarinet, you know. There was a clarinet section, you know, about three clarinets playing together, you know. But not now. There's some bands been going for years and years without a clarinet player, you know. You know that.

So it was different then. So then playing slow, then that came in vogue. And, well, jazz was expanding then. I would say that. There was more people playing it and more people who -- who I would say more people who were -- I think the interest was larger. Like now, there are a whole lot of musicians who are interested in jazz. I think more than ever. Now, I think, even though the public is slow to realize about jazz. But every day -- I mean in my going around playing, like the young people, there are more and more young people who are just discovering jazz, and I think that in time to come jazz will really -- will be really the thing, as opposed to rock and roll or whatever.
You're getting a lot of young people out of the West End, I guess.
Oh, yes, sure. And they love it. They love it. They love it. Uh-huh.
